grants.purpose: Control and restore the tty or console
grants.admits: Ordinary teardown is serialized. Output failures can enter panic cleanup under an already-held guard.
grants.narrowestForm: Serialize only the private rendering and teardown paths without holding the guard while waiting for input
grants.whyNoNarrower: Control and restore the tty or console
grants.order: DRAWING precedes restore; cancellation writes before exit. Rust panic hooks run before the guard can release.

grants.purpose: Keep owned buffers bounded where possible and wipe them on normal exit
grants.admits: Locking can fail. WASM cannot lock browser memory. The host controls display and copies
grants.narrowestForm: Keep secrets in SPC or wiping buffers and avoid unnecessary copies
grants.whyNoNarrower: Keep owned buffers bounded where possible and wipe them on normal exit
grants.order: Ordinary inputs are capped before worker transfer; the growable-view case remains open.

grants.purpose: Execute browser Argon2 and pass secret bytes to wiping worker owners
grants.admits: The embedding page and browser own the execution environment
grants.narrowestForm: Keep the native and WASM engines separate. Use worker ownership, wiping and termination as documented
grants.whyNoNarrower: Execute browser Argon2 and pass secret bytes to wiping worker owners
grants.order: Owned request arrays are wiped before the terminal message.

grants.admits: The build produces the artifact accepted by downstream jobs
grants.narrowestForm: Give builder read access only; isolate the final canonical build stage
grants.order: Produce the checksum digest in the building job.

grants.purpose: Issue build provenance and make a draft
grants.admits: Attestation and draft have publication authority over the exact canonical set. Curated notes travel separately.
grants.narrowestForm: Keep OIDC and attestation rights in their own job, plus contents-write in the draft job, with a verified exact file set
grants.whyNoNarrower: Issue build provenance and make a draft
grants.order: Both jobs recheck exact names and hashes against the anchored manifest before their write operations. Tag-job execution is pending.

grants.purpose: Start the program in an extracted archive
grants.admits: The launcher binds to an executable next to the script. No Windows wrapper execution is credited.
grants.narrowestForm: Start the executable by an explicit path within the package directory
grants.whyNoNarrower: The wrapper needs only its adjacent program
grants.order: The batch script stops on an unavailable directory before calling the explicit sibling path.

findings.title: Terminal write failure can deadlock panic cleanup
findings.reproduction: Static exact-source control-flow or contract review. No vulnerability reproduction was run.
findings.expected: The affected boundary preserves the documented terminal, OS handle, build or public API contract.
findings.observed: anstream 1.0.0 panics on stderr write errors other than BrokenPipe. Private rendering and final cancellation can invoke it while holding DRAWING. The synchronous installed panic hook calls restore_and_exit, which blocks acquiring the same guard before unwind or abort can release it.
findings.impact: An ordinary terminal or diagnostic I/O error can prevent cancellation or leave terminal recovery incomplete. Static control flow independently confirmed. The previous screen-transition race is fixed and the failure mode here is distinct.
findings.recommendedFix: Make all writes in the guarded rendering and cancellation paths fallible and prevent panic cleanup from blocking on a guard the panicking thread already holds.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on its relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: Other invalid inherited Windows handles can reach File::from_raw_handle
findings.reproduction: Static exact-source control-flow or contract review. No vulnerability reproduction was run.
findings.expected: The affected boundary preserves the documented terminal, OS handle, build or public API contract.
findings.observed: GetStdHandle may return other unvalidated values from the standard handle table. The failed GetConsoleMode branch constructs a File after checking two sentinels. The Rust constructor requires an open handle.
findings.impact: A non-sentinel invalid handle can still violate the unsafe precondition. Both named sentinel cases now pass exact Windows tests. No runtime corruption was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Use non-owning Win32 reads with checked results and preserve EOF semantics, or obtain a validated handle with an appropriate ownership contract.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on its relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: Manual packaging fails with the system Bash on macOS
findings.reproduction: Static exact-source control-flow or contract review. No vulnerability reproduction was run.
findings.expected: The affected boundary preserves the documented terminal, OS handle, build or public API contract.
findings.observed: The new manifest step uses mapfile, a Bash 4 builtin. macOS system Bash is 3.2. The script implements Darwin packaging and documents GNU archive tools but has no equivalent Bash version check.
findings.impact: A supported manual packaging invocation on a Mac can write archives and then stop before writing a checksum manifest. The canonical Ubuntu build passes.
findings.recommendedFix: Collect the sorted names using a Bash-3-compatible read loop or explicitly require a newer Bash and check it before producing files.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on its relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: The documented release verification block can return success after a failed archive
findings.reproduction: Static exact-source control-flow or contract review. No vulnerability reproduction was run.
findings.expected: The affected boundary preserves the documented terminal, OS handle, build or public API contract.
findings.observed: The shell snippet runs the hash check separately and loops over archive attestations without fail-fast or aggregated failure status.
findings.impact: A copy-pasted automated check can report the final iteration's status even when an earlier archive verification failed. Explicit maintainers reviewing output can still notice the failure.
findings.recommendedFix: Make hash, source and every archive verification fail closed before any signing steps.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on its relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: Unix terminal documentation overstates cancellation and input cleanup
findings.reproduction: Static exact-source control-flow or contract review. No vulnerability reproduction was run.
findings.expected: The affected boundary preserves the documented terminal, OS handle, build or public API contract.
findings.observed: Terminal mode restoration no longer waits for output, but synchronous screen or diagnostic writes can still wait. Input that arrives between input flush and mode restoration can go to the next reader, as the implementation comment states.
findings.impact: The public guarantees of immediate completion and no carryover from a remaining paste exceed the properties established by the new mode cleanup.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe non-draining mode restoration, and state the limits for synchronous terminal output and bytes arriving after the flush.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on its relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: Release notes give the wrong public error for onNoLength
findings.reproduction: Static exact-source control-flow or contract review. No vulnerability reproduction was run.
findings.expected: The affected boundary preserves the documented terminal, OS handle, build or public API contract.
findings.observed: The draft describes a TypeError as the rejected operation's public outcome. Exact browser logs and the browser guide show CALLBACK_FAILED with TypeError as its cause.
findings.impact: An integrator following the release note can handle the wrong error type.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe CALLBACK_FAILED and its cause consistently with the browser guide.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on its relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: Positive wallet-check evidence bypasses the documented no-length callback
findings.reproduction: Static exact-source control-flow or contract review. No vulnerability reproduction was run.
findings.expected: The affected boundary preserves the documented terminal, OS handle, build or public API contract.
findings.observed: When detection finds no length, a positive 16-bit wallet check can cause the worker to return before calling onNoLength even when there is no verified match. The callback contract describes detection finding no length as the condition.
findings.impact: A caller may wait for the opportunity to supply a stronger address or fingerprint reference that the worker never requests. The result itself remains unverified.
findings.recommendedFix: Follow the no-length callback contract for that path or explicitly document the intended exception and preserve the unverified outcome.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on its relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

reviewNotes: The previous run at 8172495 failed the browser job and both macOS portable jobs. The final run at e644260 passes after checking the CALLBACK_FAILED wrapper and excluding the system-managed PENDIN state from termios comparison.
The HTTP fuzzer could additionally check that the parsed head equals the whole structured input. The required-success and 16 KiB boundary repair addresses the original defect.
An earlier RustSec run is retained for identical locked inputs, manifest and workflow bytes. It is not a fresh advisory scan on this revision.
AUD-050-BLD001 retains its source-evidence disposition. This branch workflow supplies no attest or draft execution on a signed tag.

remediation.evidence: The earlier screen flag-to-write race is serialized. Named lock regression passes on both Linux architectures, both Windows toolchains and both macOS architectures. The test covers lock ownership, while protected cancellation mode and transitions are also traced in source. A distinct panic path is AUD-052-SEC001.

The Unix restore path now flushes input and sets modes immediately, retrying each interrupted call. The focused test passes on both Linux and both macOS runners. The initial Mac test compared the kernel PENDIN bit; the final test masks that bit. Output writes and newly arriving input are separate, see AUD-052-DOC002.

Owned request arrays are wiped before the terminal result and error messages in worker-runtime; callback-owned arrays retain their separate cleanup. Browser suites pass, but no direct scheduling or observed wipe receipt was retained.

The search owns indices and candidate indices in Zeroizing. Candidate text is assembled within a reserved string without a temporary vector of word references. Retained native/browser functional coverage does not inspect post-drop bytes.
Both sentinel branches have dedicated regression passes on Windows GNU and MSVC. Arbitrary malformed raw handles are a neighboring case tracked as AUD-052-SEC002.
Rust now borrows the shared page through Cow; Python writes a borrowed body. Headers and body share a deadline. Functional local-server CI passes, with no process-memory benchmark used as evidence.

The flag is published before the first unchecked word and cleared only after a successful check. Ordinary cancel scenarios pass. The specific unchecked or failed-check cancellation window is confirmed by source.
Rust and Python suppress bodies on HEAD errors with the GET metadata preserved. The Rust route regression and Python launcher parity are covered by exact host CI.

Exact Chrome and Firefox reject overlong repair/inspect input before the browser worker. Public Rust repair still calls card_text before core validation, and card_text reserves card.len() before filtering. Oversize padding can duplicate the input footprint even if the normalized card would be tiny. Count admitted words and useful bytes during bounded normalization before allocation.
Exact fast-mode tests cover empty method or target, mixed line terminators, error HEAD, and a manifest within the old character bound but beyond the byte bound.
Both browsers in both modes reject the forbidden walletCheck answer as CALLBACK_FAILED with a TypeError cause. New eligibility and release-note observations are tracked separately.

Position lookup resolves only against this review and returns None when it offers no repair there. The exact CI test checks the absent position and existing same-review access, through the revised CLI and wasm callers.

Recovery and confirmation carry their originating Rekey ID, validated on each receiving API before use. The exact test rejects cross-session confirm, owner_lengths_after and seal, including sessions of the same container.

The checksum input comes from the current invocation's archive list. The exact canonical build makes the same six manifest entries and the downloaded bytes match. The new system-Bash compatibility problem is AUD-052-BLD001.
The batch file stops on failed cd and calls the quoted sibling executable path. Verified statically; native Windows workflows start the binary directly, so the actual launcher was not executed.

Maintainer commands now bind the repository, workflow, tag and source commit, and document separate tag and PGP signatures. Exact tag-only execution is pending, and fail-closed command exit status is AUD-052-DOC001.

Whole structured heads must parse and near-limit heads exercise both sides of admission. Exact CI linted the harness. A maintainer-reported short run is not an independent exact-CI campaign or a coverage receipt.

The Linux fixture now enters via test-only .init_array before the Rust harness starts, with no fork and ownership transferred with into_raw_fd. Parent tests pass on exact host/ARM64 and Docker. A permitted memory/namespace refusal remains a permitted fixture result, with no independent claim that a namespace was created.

The old subclass case is closed and tested in both browsers and both modes. For an accepted length-tracking Uint8Array over a growable SharedArrayBuffer, the intrinsic getter and the copy constructor still sample length separately. Copy only the checked number of bytes via a fixed-length view, or explicitly reject such views. No concurrent test was run.

limitations: Scope is remediation, the complete diff, and touched boundaries. The rest of the wider AUD-051 project review was retained.
Hosted runtime tests exercise the checked-out source builds. Candidate archives are verified by bytes, with tagged release.yml tests, attestations and draft still pending.
The Windows batch launcher is statically verified. Windows jobs execute the binary directly. Hosted macOS signature checks cannot prove task-port denial on a SIP-enabled machine.
The full host release-profile suite, Miri, full-size vectors and browser runs, an independent second canonical rebuild, and a full hosted fuzz/coverage round were not newly executed.
The machine was at 93–94 Celsius, above the heavy-work limit. The workspace cap for local fuzz is 30 seconds per run. New findings use static evidence.
